events.title: Elizabeth I Becomes Queen of England
events.description: Upon the death of her half-sister Mary I, the 25-year-old Elizabeth became queen of England. She was proclaimed at Westminster, and the news was met with widespread celebration.
events.significance: Her 44-year reign, the Elizabethan era, shaped English religion, culture and naval power. Her accession day was celebrated in England for generations.

events.title: Congress Meets in the Capitol for the First Time
events.description: The U.S. Congress convened in the unfinished Capitol building in Washington, D.C. It was the first session held in the new permanent capital.
events.significance: The meeting marked the federal government's move to its permanent home, and the Capitol has been the seat of Congress ever since.

events.title: The Suez Canal Opens
events.description: After ten years of construction, the Suez Canal was formally inaugurated in a lavish ceremony. It linked the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea.
events.significance: The canal cut the sea journey between Europe and Asia by thousands of miles. It transformed global trade and remains one of the world's key shipping routes.

events.title: Douglas Engelbart Patents the Computer Mouse
events.description: Inventor Douglas Engelbart received a U.S. patent for an 'X-Y position indicator for a display system'. This was the device we now call the computer mouse.
events.significance: The mouse made graphical computer interfaces practical. It changed how people interact with computers.

events.title: Nixon Declares 'I Am Not a Crook'
events.description: At a question-and-answer session with newspaper editors, President Richard Nixon responded to Watergate-era questions about his finances. He said he was not a crook.
events.significance: The line became one of the best-known quotes of the Watergate scandal. It is often cited as a symbol of the collapse of public trust in Nixon's presidency.
